round_1.summary: The script's mechanics are sound. It imports no producer code, its checks catch every mutation I tried, it holds RLIMIT_AS at 768 MiB, and a re-run on AB01/d10 reproduced the worker's numbers exactly. It goes back because the shared cutPoints assumption is wrong for this record. Bounded source reads show that the cutPoints index the treadmill velocity-profile clock (cvel), not the joint clock. On AB01/d10 that clock is offset by about 1.65 to 1.9 s from the joint, marker, forceplate and heel-strike clock. The pilot's task windows are therefore shifted. The audit reproduces them and reports pass with only a flag. On AB01/d10 this mislabels 8 of the 18 transition strides and changes 39 to 44 of the 260 pair decisions.

cutpoint_ruling.ruling: blocking for the AB01/d10 pilot's task labels and exclusions, and for any claim that the audit validated them. It is not blocking for the audit's value, side, phase, clock-unit or receipt checks, which hold.
evidence: Source layout (AB01/d10, bounded h5py metadata reads): joint, marker channels 16193 frames; forceplates 161930 (= 10 x 16193); events/VelProf/cvel 16295 samples; cutPoints max 16294.

cutPoints index the cvel clock: every cutPoint edge coincides with a cvel ramp edge to within one sample (s0x8 starts where cvel stops being NaN at 1828; s1 [5049, 8048] and s1x2 [8272, 11271] are flat at 1.000 and 1.200; each transition interval spans exactly one cvel ramp, e.g. d0x2 [15667, 16294] goes from 1.2 to 0).

Heel strikes are on the joint and forceplate clock. Source LHS and RHS sit within 0.4 and 0.05 joint frames (median) of left and right forceplate force onsets, with 87% and 90% within 2 frames. This also gives independent physical-side evidence: LHS goes with the left plate and RHS with the right plate.

Belt speed was estimated independently from the heel and toe marker AP velocity 15-30 frames after each source heel strike, on the joint clock, and compared with cvel at index = joint frame + lag. The probe was run on transition periods ±3 s. On AB01/d10 the best lag is +165 frames (median error 0.046 m/s); at lag 0 the error is 0.247 m/s. Around a0x2, the belt reaches 1.25 m/s by joint frame 14988, while cvel at the same index is 0.86 and does not reach 1.2 until 15166.

Controls show the method finds lag near 0 where the clocks agree: AB02/d10 +10, AB03/d10 +12, AB05/d10 +11, AB08/d10 -2, AB01/i0 +17, AB01/i10 -9 (errors 0.01-0.08 m/s, lag-0 error within 0.004 m/s of best). AB01 is anomalous: d10 +165, d5 +684, i5 -404.

Separate source anomaly: AB01/i5 and AB01/i10 contain identical jointAngles (RHipAngles bitwise equal) and identical RHS, but different cutPoints. Only i10's cutPoints fit the kinematics, which suggests the i5 kinematics are a copy of i10.

Impact on AB01/d10: if the cutPoints are shifted into joint frames by lag 165 (or 190), 39 (or 44) of 260 pairs change classification. All 4 pilot a0x5 strides and 4 of 10 a0x2 strides fall outside a transition (the belt is already at a steady 1.2 m/s). About 3 strides per steady-speed condition move across each window edge. Previously excluded pairs become d0x2 (4), d0x5 (2) and a0x2/a0x5 (7). Exclusions fall from 77 to 72 (lag 165) or 71 (lag 190).
cutpoint_ruling.proposed_independent_check: Add a check named, for example, 'clock_cut_points_aligned_with_joint_frames' to the audit. For each source heel strike h, belt speed = |mean AP velocity of that side's HEE and TOE markers over joint frames h+15..h+29| (central difference x 100 Hz; AP axis = the axis with the largest median |velocity|). Compare with cvel[h+22+lag-1] over the transition intervals ±300 frames, for lags in [-1000, 1000]. State in advance: pass only if the best lag is within ±50 frames AND the lag-0 median error is within 0.02 m/s of the best. Otherwise fail. Do not flag. Report the best lag and both errors. Reads are bounded: 4 marker arrays of 0.5 MiB each plus cvel; peak RSS was 46 MiB in the reviewer probe. Do not shift cutPoints in the audit; the alignment rule is José's call (see decision_for_jose).

PM-01 says to re-hash every file in its bindings.

Make report writing fail closed with exit 2. Today json.dumps(allow_nan=False) runs after open(..., 'x'). A NaN reaching the report (for example a NaN cutPoint feeding clock.cut_points_max) would leave an empty audit_report.json and exit 1 through an uncaught ValueError. Serialize first, then open and write, and return 2 on failure.

Record a known limit, or handle it: the producer's np.gradient on linspace times uses the non-uniform 3-point formula, which includes f[i]. The audit's central difference skips f[i]. For a lone NaN sample (possible only when a stride exceeds 149 frames), the masks would differ. The audit would fail closed, not pass wrongly. Similar fail-closed divergence: linspace positions vs exact rational positions next to a NaN frame. Not reachable on AB01/d10 (no NaN).

decision_for_jose.note: Drafted for the coordinator to copy into backlog.json; the reviewer did not edit backlog.json. Proposed as a high-stakes convention item (decide_before_recommendation true).
decision_for_jose.question: The treadmill task intervals in the UM21 source run on the belt-speed clock. For some AB01 recordings that clock is offset by up to several seconds from the motion data. How should treadmill strides be assigned to tasks?

options.label: Exclude misaligned recordings
options.consequence: Recordings whose belt-speed/motion offset exceeds 0.5 s (AB01 d10, d5, i5 among those checked) lose task labels and are left out; cheap, reversible.

options.label: Re-align by measured offset
options.consequence: Task intervals are shifted by an offset measured from the marker belt speed for each recording; keeps the data but adds a new derived step that needs its own review; reversible.

options.label: Keep source intervals as published
options.consequence: No change; about 15% of AB01/d10 pair decisions and 8 of its 18 transition strides stay mislabelled.

decision_for_jose.cost_of_waiting: The UM21 treadmill pilot and the 50-record treadmill release stay blocked. Other datasets are unaffected.
decision_for_jose.recommended: A for the pilot now (choose a pilot record whose clocks agree, e.g. AB02/d10 at lag +10), B considered later with its own review
decision_for_jose.why: The offset is large and clearly measured on AB01, while other subjects line up within about 0.2 s. Excluding is conservative and invents nothing; re-aligning is a new estimate.
decision_for_jose.check: In AB01 d10, the belt is already at full speed (1.25 m/s from the markers) at motion frame 14988, while the source's acceleration interval does not end until 15166.
decision_for_jose.related_finding: AB01 i5 and i10 contain identical motion data with different task intervals; i5's motion appears to be a copy of i10. Needs its own scope decision for the 50-record treadmill release.
